Matt — thanks for the concrete examples, and for the sample file. High level first: we bill input tokens (everything the model receives for tokenization: user messages, system messages, and any tool outputs that are re-inserted as model input) and output tokens (tokens produced by the model as assistant output). Tool outputs that are produced outside the model (e.g., an external search API that returns text inserted verbatim) are counted as output tokens at the moment they are emitted to you.

Subject: Re: Clarify token counting for our SOW (system/tool/KV-cache examples) — formal breakdown

Hi Matt — thanks for the sample and the patience. Below is a formalized breakdown you can drop into an SOW or contract addendum; I've included short examples tied to the sample rows you sent. If you want this converted to legal language we can hand it to Contracts, but this is our practical metering policy for hosted API baseline.

Summary (short):
- Input tokens: any tokens that are passed into the model tokenizer as part of the request. This includes user messages, system messages, and tool outputs that the model receives as input for further decoding.
- Output tokens: tokens produced by the model decoder that are returned as assistant text (streamed or final).
- Tool tokens: tokens generated by external tools (search, database, code-exec) are billed as output tokens at the time they are emitted to the client. If those tool outputs are subsequently passed back into the model for further generation, they are also counted as input tokens for that follow-up request.
- Rounding: token counts are integer token counts per request after tokenization. For streaming responses we accumulate generated tokens continuously; billing is based on the sum of generated tokens emitted to the client, rounded up to the next whole token. There are no fractional-token credits.
- KV-prefix cache behavior:
  - When a cached prefix is reused to accelerate decoding but the model still performs decoding steps for additional tokens, we bill for all tokens that the model decodes (i.e., those that required compute). 
  - If a response is served entirely from a cache snapshot without invoking model decoding (exact match / cold-start skirted by a previously stored response), we treat that as a cache-hit delivery: the customer is billed for a small per-delivery cache-retrieval charge rather than the standard per-output-token compute charge. Cache retrievals are currently billed at $0.00005 per retrieval for hosted API baseline (waived for customers with >$50k/month committed usage under the negotiated discount program).
  - In short: you are not charged full decode compute for repeated identical responses; you may still see a small cache retrieval line item if the response was delivered from cache.

Line-by-line example (from your CSV):
Row A: [system: 40 tokens] + [user prompt: 320 tokens] -> model generates [assistant: 450 tokens]
- Input billed: 360 tokens (system + user)
- Output billed: 450 tokens
- Total billed (for metering): 810 tokens

Row B (tool chain): [system: 20] + [user: 60] -> model calls tool -> tool returns 500 tokens -> model ingests tool output and generates 120 tokens final
- Input billed: 580 tokens (system + user + tool output passed to model)
- Output billed: 120 tokens (assistant final) + 500 tokens (tool emission billed at emission time) = 620 tokens
- Total billed: 1,200 tokens

Row C (KV prefix hit): user prompt maps to cached response snapshot (exact match) — no model decoding invoked
- Input billed: user tokens as usual
- Output billed: cache-retrieval fee (per-delivery) instead of per-output-token compute charges (see policy above)

Pricing (baseline hosted API examples) — illustrative only; final numbers will come from contracts/addendum: 
- Baseline list prices: $0.002 per 1K input tokens, $0.006 per 1K output tokens. (This is the public non-committed rate on our current rate card PDF.)
- Cache retrieval fee (hosted baseline): $0.00005 per retrieval (first 10M cache retrievals free under commitment tier; otherwise charged).

Discounting guidance (examples for your SOW planning):
- 10% discount on token unit prices for $50k/mo committed spend (12-month)
- 18% discount for $150k/mo committed spend (12-month) plus 30-day priority SLA
- Custom elastic pricing and additional cache-waiver options available for >$300k/mo commitments — we can model economics in the billing-matrix-BOA.csv attached.

Notes & edge cases:
- Partial tool emissions: if a streaming tool returns partial text that is then consumed by the model, we meter the tool emission tokens at emission time and the tokens consumed as input when re-ingested. This can double-count in the simple sense (emission + later input) — we call this out in SOWs and can offer a contract credit mechanism for high-volume tool-chaining patterns.
- Function-call metadata (JSON wrappers): wrapper tokens for structured tool call metadata are counted as input when sent to the model; they are negligible typically but important at scale.
- Billing transparency: we provide per-request token logs for reconciliation; customers on Dedicated or Private can opt into raw metering exports.

Next steps: If the above aligns with your procurement team's needs, we will draft SOW language and a short addendum that codifies: (a) token definitions, (b) cache retrieval fee and thresholds, (c) discount tier and commitment period, and (d) reconciliation process.

If you want, we can also produce a sample-month invoice mock using your 10M tokens and the different discount scenarios — I can run that and attach by COB Thursday if you confirm the QPS and tool-usage mix.
